Healthy.fertilizer: Maintain routine balanced NPK (e.g. 10-10-10) schedule per tree age; add organic compost/farmyard manure annually
Healthy.cultural_practice: Continue regular monitoring, proper spacing, and irrigation scheduling

Anthracnose.pesticide: Carbendazim 50% WP (1 g/L water) or Copper oxychloride (3 g/L) sprayed at 10-15 day intervals
Anthracnose.fertilizer: Balanced NPK with adequate potassium to strengthen tissue resistance; avoid excess nitrogen which promotes soft, susceptible growth
Anthracnose.cultural_practice: Prune and destroy infected twigs and fallen leaves; avoid overhead/sprinkler irrigation; improve canopy airflow
Anthracnose.severity_note: Repeat spray through flowering and fruit development stages, especially in humid weather

Bacterial Canker.pesticide: Copper-based bactericide (Copper oxychloride 3 g/L or Streptocycline 0.5 g/L) sprayed every 10-15 days
Bacterial Canker.fertilizer: Balanced NPK; avoid excess nitrogen; ensure adequate potassium and calcium for cell wall strength
Bacterial Canker.cultural_practice: Remove and burn severely infected branches; disinfect pruning tools between cuts; avoid working on wet foliage
Bacterial Canker.severity_note: Spray preventively before monsoon/rainy season when bacterial spread is highest

Cutting Weevil.cause: Insect pest (Deporaus marginatus - mango leaf-cutting weevil)
Cutting Weevil.pesticide: Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (2.5 ml/L) or Quinalphos 25% EC (2 ml/L) sprayed on new flush
Cutting Weevil.fertilizer: Avoid excessive nitrogen which triggers flushes of tender new leaves that attract the weevil
Cutting Weevil.cultural_practice: Collect and destroy fallen cut leaf pieces (larvae develop inside them); time sprays with new flush emergence
Cutting Weevil.severity_note: Monitor closely during the vegetative flush period

Die Back.pesticide: Carbendazim 50% WP (1 g/L) as a spray, plus paste application (Bordeaux paste) on cut wounds
Die Back.fertilizer: Improve overall tree vigor with balanced NPK plus micronutrients (zinc, boron); avoid water stress
Die Back.cultural_practice: Prune dead/dying twigs well below the affected area and seal cuts; avoid mechanical injury to bark
Die Back.severity_note: Address promptly - dieback can progress into main branches if untreated

Gall Midge.pesticide: Dimethoate 30% EC (2 ml/L) or Monocrotophos 36% SL sprayed at bud break and again after 15 days
Gall Midge.fertilizer: Balanced NPK; avoid over-fertilizing with nitrogen during flowering flush
Gall Midge.cultural_practice: Deep ploughing under the tree canopy to expose and kill soil-pupating larvae; remove and destroy infested leaves/flowers
Gall Midge.severity_note: Time sprays to coincide with new leaf/panicle emergence

Powdery Mildew.pesticide: Wettable sulphur (2-3 g/L) or Hexaconazole 5% EC (1 ml/L) sprayed at 10-day intervals, starting at flowering
Powdery Mildew.fertilizer: Balanced NPK; avoid excess nitrogen; ensure adequate potassium for disease resistance
Powdery Mildew.cultural_practice: Prune for better light penetration and airflow; avoid dense canopy and high humidity around flowers
Powdery Mildew.severity_note: Most damaging during flowering - can cause major fruit-set loss if untreated

Sooty Mould.cause: Fungal (Capnodium mangiferae), growing on honeydew secreted by sap-sucking insects (hoppers, mealybugs)
Sooty Mould.pesticide: Control underlying insect first: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (0.3 ml/L); wash mould off with a mild starch/soap solution spray
Sooty Mould.fertilizer: Standard balanced NPK - mould itself doesn't need fertilizer intervention, controlling the insect vector matters more
Sooty Mould.cultural_practice: Manage honeydew-producing pests (hoppers/mealybugs); improve airflow to reduce humidity
Sooty Mould.severity_note: Treat the insect infestation, not just the visible black mould, or it will recur

Healthy.fertilizer: Routine balanced NPK plus organic manure; neem is generally low-maintenance once established
Healthy.cultural_practice: Maintain normal watering and monitoring schedule

Alternaria.pesticide: Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5 g/L) or Chlorothalonil sprayed at 10-14 day intervals
Alternaria.fertilizer: Balanced NPK with adequate potassium; avoid nitrogen excess
Alternaria.cultural_practice: Remove and destroy fallen infected leaves; avoid overhead irrigation late in the day

Dieback.pesticide: Carbendazim 50% WP (1 g/L) spray plus wound-paste application on cut branches
Dieback.fertilizer: Improve vigor with balanced NPK and micronutrients; avoid drought stress
Dieback.cultural_practice: Prune affected branches below the visible damage and seal cuts; avoid mechanical wounding
Dieback.severity_note: Treat early - dieback spreads down the branch toward the trunk

Leaf blight.pesticide: Copper oxychloride (3 g/L) or Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) sprayed at 10-15 day intervals
Leaf blight.fertilizer: Balanced NPK; ensure adequate potassium for resistance
Leaf blight.cultural_practice: Remove infected leaf litter; improve canopy spacing and airflow
Leaf blight.severity_note: Most severe in warm, humid conditions

Leaf miners.cause: Insect pest (leaf-mining moth/fly larvae tunneling inside leaf tissue)
Leaf miners.pesticide: Neem oil (5 ml/L, ironically effective here) or Spinosad 45% SC (0.3 ml/L)
Leaf miners.fertilizer: Standard balanced NPK; healthy vigorous growth tolerates minor mining damage better
Leaf miners.cultural_practice: Remove and destroy heavily mined leaves; encourage natural parasitoid wasps as biological control
Leaf miners.severity_note: Damage is mostly cosmetic unless infestation is severe

Leaf miners_Powdery mildew.cause: Combined insect (leaf miner) and fungal (powdery mildew) infestation
Leaf miners_Powdery mildew.pesticide: Wettable sulphur (2-3 g/L) for mildew + Neem oil (5 ml/L) or Spinosad for miners; apply separately, 5-7 days apart
Leaf miners_Powdery mildew.fertilizer: Balanced NPK; avoid nitrogen excess which favors both pest and mildew
Leaf miners_Powdery mildew.cultural_practice: Improve airflow/light penetration; remove affected leaves
Leaf miners_Powdery mildew.severity_note: Treat both issues - controlling only one allows the other to persist

Powdery mildew.pesticide: Wettable sulphur (2-3 g/L) or Hexaconazole 5% EC (1 ml/L) at 10-day intervals
Powdery mildew.cultural_practice: Prune for airflow; avoid excess humidity around foliage
Powdery mildew.severity_note: Spray at first sign of white powdery patches before it spreads

Healthy.fertilizer: Routine balanced NPK plus organic manure appropriate to tree age
Healthy.cultural_practice: Maintain normal watering and monitoring schedule
